messages:
maria: heads up — we're seeing a spike of 429s for /v1/generate in prod-eu starting ~2026-03-18T10:05Z. Counts jump ~18x, errors concentrated in two orgs. suspect: tonight's quota-service rollout. @oncall please take a look

sre-bot: alert: 429 rate increased to 12/min (baseline 0.7/min) across eu region. linked grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rrq-usage/ratelimit?orgId=1 :rotating_light:

jon: looking. quick grep across quota configs — org_42 and org_88 have burst_window_ms set to 0 after the config-sanitizer change. that's probably the regression.

kevin: ack. we merged the sanitizer PR at 10:01Z that coerces missing burst_window_ms -> 0 instead of leaving it unset. that was intended to be safe but yeah, it disables burst semantics. my bad.

ash: copying some router traces — when per-org limiter returns `REJECT`, router tries fallback pool (global-shared) immediately. fallback pool has a lower per-key burst allowance and stricter per-minute quotas. some SDKs are also configured with immediate retry (no jitter) for 5xx only, so they hit 429 -> client-side retry -> more 429s. looks like a cascade.

kevin: sample config for org_42 from consul (10:03Z):
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_42",
  "rate_limit": { "requests_per_minute": 1200, "burst_window_ms": 0 }
}
```

jon: that 0 is the problem — effectively disables token-bucket burst. requests that normally would be allowed in short bursts get rejected and then funneled to fallback which is lower capacity.

ash: mitigation options: 1) revert sanitizer to leave unset (old behavior) 2) hotpatch default to 1000ms for burst_window_ms 3) add router guard to avoid fallback to a strictly lower-tier pool within Xs of rejection. i think we should do 2 + 3 asap.

kevin: pushing config-revert patch to config-repo now to restore previous sanitizer behavior and add explicit default of 1000ms. patch: `config-sanitizer: set default.burst_window_ms = 1000`

deploy-bot: deploy started: config-revert by kevin (ci/job/4528) -> staging -> prod-eu canary

jon: also sending a quick router change: if fallback_pool.capacity_score < primary.capacity_score then don't fallback for 30s after per-org reject. small safeguard to prevent downgrade loops. will open PR and flag for hotfix review.

ash: rolling metrics: within 6m of the revert canary, 429 spike dropped from 12/min -> 1.1/min. p95 latency stable.

kevin: revert merged and promoted to prod-eu at 10:22Z. verified consul configs now show burst_window_ms = 1000 for affected orgs.

maria: great. @ops please monitor for next 2 hours. we'll create a short postmortem outlining root cause (sanitizer default drift + router fallback policy) and follow-ups.

ops: acked. creating incident doc and assigning action items: add unit test for sanitizer default, add canary gate for quota config changes, update router fallback rule and add integration test, notify SDK teams about recommended backoff config.

jon: note for postmortem — also verify SDKs that disable jitter/backoff on 4xx; we should publish guidance so clients don't immediate-retry on 429s.

maria: closing the active throttle window. will follow up with the postmortem today. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
summary: production 429 spike caused by config sanitizer defaulting burst_window_ms to 0; fallback routing to lower-tier pool amplified throttles; reverted sanitizer and added router guard; metrics normalized
